annotation_description: Haiku Analyst passed priority with 2 untapped lands and Avacyn's Pilgrim in hand. Avacyn's Pilgrim costs {G} and is a mana dork that taps for {W}, which would accelerate toward casting Sigarda, Heron's Grace or other expensive spells. On turn 2, deploying a mana dork is almost always correct as it enables turn 3 plays that would otherwise come on turn 4. There's no reason to hold back the Pilgrim here.

Bojuka Bog was used to exile Qwen3L Vorthos's apparently empty graveyard, while Gem25F Libby (likely a Golgari/graveyard-focused deck with Golgari Rot Farm) already has Cloudthresher in their graveyard as a reanimation target.

Mycoloth without any creatures to devour enters as a vanilla 4/4 that generates 0 Saproling tokens per upkeep, making it very underwhelming for its 5 mana cost. Jarad, Golgari Lich Lord was castable ({B}{B}{G}{G} available from Golgari Rot Farm + Swamp + 2 Forests) and would have been a 3/3 with a powerful sacrifice ability that synergizes with the deck's graveyard theme, plus it grows as more creatures enter the graveyard.

Cast Jarad (a 3/3 with limited utility due to no sacrifice fodder) over Mycoloth (a 4/4 that generates saproling tokens each upkeep). The reasoning incorrectly states Mycoloth isn't available/castable, but it's in hand and castable with the available mana ({3}{G}{G} from 6 available mana via Golgari Rot Farm producing 2). Mycoloth's token generation provides much better board development even without devour targets.

Mycoloth without any creatures to sacrifice to Devour is just a vanilla 4/4 with no meaningful ability. The only creature available to devour is Jarad (the commander), which would be a terrible sacrifice. Meanwhile, Butcher of Malakir (5/4 flyer with forced sacrifice trigger) was castable for exactly 7 mana (5BB) with the available lands, and would have been far more impactful.

Jarad is a 3/3 (base 2/2 + 1 from Cloudthresher in graveyard) that could attack any opponent for likely unblocked damage. Most opponents either have no blockers (Qwen3L), only flyers that can't block ground (GLM47's Tegwyll and Bladecrafter, Haiku's Sigarda), or small ground creatures that would trade poorly. Jarad's sacrifice ability ({1}{B}{G}) doesn't require him to be untapped.

GLM47 Gramps declined to attack with two evasive Faeries (Faerie Bladecrafter 2/2 flying and Nettling Nuisance 3/1 flying) when no opponent has untapped flying blockers. Attacking would deal 5 damage, put a +1/+1 counter on Faerie Bladecrafter, AND create a goaded 4/2 Pirate token for the damaged player that can't block and must attack someone other than Gramps - extremely valuable when at 9 life since it redirects aggression. All of Gramps' lands are tapped so there's no mana to hold up anyway.

Failed to play the Forest from hand before casting Butcher of Malakir. Even though the extra mana wouldn't change the plays available this turn, missing a land drop is always suboptimal - it provides information hiding and ensures you don't forget later, and the extra mana could matter on future turns if something happens at instant speed.

By letting Bonehoard resolve before casting Putrefy on Runic Armasaur, the Germ token entered as a 4/4 instead of a 5/5. Casting Putrefy in response to Bonehoard on the stack would have put Runic Armasaur into the graveyard first, increasing the creature card count in all graveyards by 1 before the Germ was created.
